texts.facts: 2. By this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the applicant is challenging the first information report dated 05.09.2020 bearing Crime No. 325/2020, registered with Police Station, Imamwada, Nagpur. Hence, notice is given to the non-applicants only in respect of the offence punishable under Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code. He also prayed for grant of stay to the further investigation by the investigating agency, as contained in prayer clause (ii). 5. The arrest was initially challenged at the Principal Seat of this Court and also it was prayed in the petition that he be released on interim bail. The said was rejected and against that, an appeal was preferred before the Hon'ble Apex Court. 17. Thereafter, the applicant approached before this Court and prayed that in the event of arrest in connection with Crime No. 325/2020, he be released on anticipatory bail. The said application was registered as Criminal Application (ABA) No. 409/2020 and though, initially vide order dated 21.09.2020, he was granted ad-interim anticipatory bail on certain conditions, ultimately after hearing the learned Additional Public Prosecutor and after perusing the reply filed on behalf of the Ankush S/O Shivnarayan Jaiswal vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Imamwada Nagpur ... on 14 December, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5632781/ 4 State opposing the prayer for pre-arrest bail, vide order dated 01.12.2020, the application for pre-arrest bail was rejected. A first information report was registered against Naval Kishore and others for the offence punishable under Section 409 of the Indian Penal Code at Hussainganj Police Station, Lucknow vide Crime No. 11/2013. The respondents before the Hon'ble Apex Court had filed a writ petition before the Allahabad High Court for quashing of the first information report and the said was dismissed on 01.02.2013. Thereafter, the charge-sheet was filed.
texts.arguments: In order to buttress his submissions, the learned senior Advocate painstakingly took us through the judgments delivered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnab Manorajan Goswami .versus. The state of Maharashtra and others in Criminal Appeal No. 742 of 2020 ; Imtiyaz Ahmad .vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others, reported in (2012) 2 SCC 688 and also in the case of Amish Devgan .vs. Union of India and others in Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 160 of 2020. He submitted that personal liberty of the applicant is most important and as observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Arnab Goswami's case, the personal liberty is the basic fabric of the Constitution of India. He, therefore, submitted that the interim order in the nature of not taking coercive steps and/or not to arrest the applicant, be granted. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. M. J. Khan strongly opposed the prayer of interim relief. In order to oppose the interim relief, he relied upon various reported decisions. He prayed that since the earlier application for pre- arrest bail filed on behalf of the applicant is already rejected 3 141220apl800.20.odt by this Court, the prayer is untenable. 7. In Arnab Goswami's case (supra), the petitioner before the Hon'ble Apex Court was arrested for the offence punishable under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code. 8. In Imtiyaz Ahmad's case (supra), the question that was posed before the Hon'ble Apex Court was regarding stay orders being granted to the investigation, FIR or trial in criminal proceedings and thereafter the matter remaining pending for years together. In such a situation, the Hon'ble Apex Court, in paragraph 55 of the said judgment observed that the power to grant stay of investigation and trial is very extraordinary power given to the High Courts and the same power is to be exercised sparingly only to prevent an abuse of the process and to promote the ends of justice. It was also 4 141220apl800.20.odt directed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the High Court should make it a point of finally disposing of such proceedings as early as possible but preferably within six months from the date the stay order is issued. 9. In Amish Devgan's case (supra) also, the Hon'ble Apex Court granted interim relief in favour of the petitioner before it. In this case, the petitioner directly invoked the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble Apex Court under Article 32 of the Constitution of India and while exercising jurisdiction under Article 32, the Hon'ble Apex Court found that the petitioner therein had made out a case and therefore, he was granted interim relief.
